question: According to Eurostat, the rate of unemployment in the Canary Islands was 13.5% in 2025, while in Europe as a whole it was 6%. The youth unemployment gap reached 14.3 percentage points. In 2024, the average annual wage per employee was EUR 35 800, compared to EUR 45 700 in the European Union. The government of Pedro Sánchez presents growth and employment records as a proof of success.

However, these figures highlight the gap between official rhetoric and the opportunities available to young people in the Canary Islands. Progress must also be measured by the possibility of finding stable employment, becoming independent and building a life for oneself without having to leave the islands. The government’s lack of connection with this generation calls for concrete responses and accountability.
Youth unemployment and the inadequate income levels call for the performance of state policies to be reviewed, in coordination with the Canarian authorities.

European funds should promote training linked to employment, diversification of production and innovation, with verifiable objectives for integration into the labour market and improved income levels The remoteness of the islands calls for tailored actions that turn young talent into career opportunities. 1.
What verifiable results have the ESF + and the Youth Guarantee achieved in the Canary Islands?
Will the Commission call on the Spanish Government to set targets for reducing youth unemployment and improving incomes?
What actions will it promote to diversify the economy, retain talent and help young people to become independent in the Canary Islands?
